findings.title: Database operation control prototypes disagreed with the fixed Core operation contract

evidence.observed_before_fix: request_cancel and try_retire had an extra nw_error_info_v1* argument; operation_release returned nw_status and accepted an error argument.

evidence.observation: Fixed roles require cancel(op), retire(op), and void release(op); C-ASYNC-001 section 3 has the same exact shape.

findings.impact: Two normative generation inputs would produce incompatible imports and destructor behavior. Release failure did not establish who retained ownership.
findings.remediation: The Database author removed the two diagnostic arguments, made operation_release void, and stated OK-only cancellation, OK/PENDING retirement, Created-or-Retired release with no live calls, and no callbacks/unwind/blocking join.

recheck.result: The corrected prototypes and postconditions agree with Core section 6.2 and C-ASYNC-001 section 3.

findings.title: The NuGet Minimal HTTP journey mapped routes on the wrong stage

evidence.observed_before_fix: Builder -> routes -> Build -> Run contradicted the declared NativeServer route extension surface.

findings.impact: A reader following the package entry guide would try unavailable builder mapping methods.
findings.remediation: The NuGet author changed the journey to configure builder -> Build() -> map routes on NativeServer -> RunAsync and documented first-start route freeze.

recheck.result: The current row matches the existing declarations and route-freeze rule. This is a review of the NuGet journey, not self-approval of the Server domain.

findings.title: The long-term package rule contradicted the selected Core extension seam

evidence.observed_before_fix: Maintainer-only contracts were required to have both a separate namespace and a separate package.

evidence.observation: NativeWeave.Interop.Extensibility is deliberately shipped in NativeWeave.Core; the NuGet graph and policies agree.

findings.impact: An adopting implementation could unnecessarily split the shared ownership seam or fail its own standard despite following the reviewed package graph.
findings.remediation: The standard author required namespace separation, made package separation depend on optional dependencies/tooling, and recorded the BCL-only Core seam rationale and continued SPI compatibility review.

recheck.result: The explicit cost/dependency decision reconciles the standard, package graph and type policies without weakening SPI review.

findings.title: Immutable database buffer destruction still has an ambiguous error and ownership shape

evidence.observation: nw_db_buffer_release_v1(nw_db_buffer*, nw_error_info_v1*) returns nw_status; the later paragraph says creating-module-only/once but does not define failed release ownership.
NativeBuffer.Dispose maps to a private SafeHandle invoking buffer_release_v1(owner) exactly once; the destructor must be nonblocking/nonthrowing/free-threaded.

findings.impact: The owner wrapper cannot infer whether a failed destructor consumed the buffer, may be retried, or leaves retained memory; the exact binding shape is inconsistent across the two normative inputs.
findings.remediation: The Database author changed buffer_release and owner_release to void/no-error destructors, reserved cleanup-ledger capacity at owner creation, made valid release consume once without retry/callback/blocking join/unwind, and retained explicit Close as the error-reporting path. NativeBufferFactory accepts only the compatible immutable free-threaded destructor.

recheck.result: Read the revised normative prototypes and ownership postconditions. They agree with Core sections 5 and 6.1; no fallible destructor ownership ambiguity remains. Other Database wire refinements are outside this review.

findings.title: The package probe protects its work directory but not an existing evidence directory

evidence.observation: A nonempty work-directory is rejected, but output.mkdir(exist_ok=True), summary.write_text and log.write_text can overwrite a previous --output when a caller supplies a different fresh work directory.

findings.impact: The existing four attempts are separate, intact and hash-verified; a later reproduction could accidentally overwrite historical evidence. This is not a defect in the observed successful run.
findings.remediation: Reject a nonempty evidence output directory as well. If repairing now, preserve the exact attempt-4 executable source as a snapshot and label the new guard as unexecuted rather than changing historical input hashes.

findings.title: Several cold metadata and asynchronous argument contracts are not exact

evidence.observation: Catalog, manifest and option snapshots are called bounded without a collection limit. Get/TryGet reject malformed engine IDs, but the manifest says only nonempty and the XML says lower-case; no exact grammar/length is assigned.
CopyToAsync lists validation/cancellation behavior but not whether argument errors are synchronous or represented by a faulted task; the precedence of pre-cancellation and empty input is not fixed.
The normative standard explicitly requires argument-validation delivery and deterministic zero/cancellation behavior.

findings.impact: Different conforming-looking implementations could accept incompatible descriptor identities or unbounded enumeration, and consumers cannot predict when an invalid async call throws. These are cold/public behavior gaps, not a request for another runtime abstraction.
findings.remediation: The Interop author specified one 1-128 byte ASCII engine-ID grammar, catalog<=256, manifest assets/capability definitions<=64 with cumulative UTF-8<=64KiB and per-field limits, options<=64 unique requirements, streaming count/size checks and no partial publication. CopyToAsync now specifies synchronous usage validation/admission, token-associated pre-cancellation before empty success, returned-task error delivery, and full write retirement before lease release. Follow-up corrections retain the exact descriptors parameter name and account for allocation of the canceled Task.

recheck.result: Read both new semantic paragraphs and the follow-up corrections. Counts/grammar/rejection and async ordering are now exact; no declaration change or new native execution claim was made.

findings.title: Generated reference omits consumption-affecting parameter and return attributes

evidence.observation: Only symbol.GetAttributes() is exported. Parameter.GetAttributes() and method return-type attributes are omitted.
The descriptor parameter has nullable/ref metadata but no NotNullWhen(true) attribute. The generated reference also lacks it, although Interop.cs declares it.
The inventory explicitly requires attributes affecting consumption.

findings.impact: Consumers reading the exact reference cannot see the compiler-enforced nullable flow contract. The generated baseline cannot detect changes to that annotation.
findings.remediation: Export parameter/return attributes and render consumption-affecting annotations in the reference, regenerate, and compare the known TryGet case against its declaration.

findings.title: Generated declarations omit type modifiers, delegate signatures and enum values

evidence.observation: The generated declaration is class NativeWeave.Interop.NativeBuffer; public sealed is absent. The JSON has accessibility separately but no sealed/static/abstract field.
The generated declaration contains only delegate and type name, without return type or parameter list.
Member display flags are insufficient to include named-type modifiers; delegateStyle remains its name-only default.
The row and rendered reference omit the value 5; no ConstantValue or enum underlying type is exported, so a numeric enum change is invisible to this baseline.

findings.impact: The advertised exact declaration reference misstates inheritance availability and does not present a usable delegate signature, contrary to the complete symbol inventory contract. It also cannot detect changes to the numeric values of managed public enum fields.
findings.remediation: Render full named-type accessibility/modifiers and delegate return/parameter signatures, retain exact base/interface/constraint metadata, regenerate and inspect representative class/record/delegate cases. Export enum underlying types and field/const values and render their exact values.

observations.result: All 31 command-log entries across attempts 1-4 match their recorded SHA256; 15 unique byte contents were read. Failed attempts retain CS0201, CS1701 and the Python tuple/list failure, without being relabeled successful.
Attempt 4 summary digest matches artifact-readback. All seven executable source inputs and two additional C header/probe inputs match their recorded SHA256 at review time.

Read all three retained nupkg entry lists/nuspecs: only facade is directly referenced; facade has exact native/build-assets dependency ranges; generator exists only under tools with one buildTransitive import; no ProjectReference shortcut or Rust build hook.

JIT output, RID-free ordinary publish and explicit-RID AOT native asset all equal the inherited codec SHA256. RID-free ordinary publish correctly retains runtimes/linux-x64/native, whereas AOT output is flattened; no current product loader implementation is claimed.

The actual retained AOT executable is an x86-64 ELF, its bytes and .dbg/native bytes match artifact-readback, and independent execution from another working directory with only /usr/bin:/bin on PATH returned exit 0. No native rebuild was performed.

The 12 cached runtime source files match their manifest digests. Critical review rereads covered NativeLibrary.cs 1-115 and 195-245, SafeHandle.cs 85-190 and CancellationTokenRegistration.cs 20-135. Other authored source read scopes are inherited, not falsely reported as new complete source audits.

The loader distinguishes one content identity per Engine from separate domain instances, failed post-load residency from retryable pre-load absence, and AOT native loading from unsupported new managed assembly loading. Core starts no domain runtime. Buffer staging counts an exact <=64KiB array; cancellation and Task completion do not retire native owners.

Standards retain exact per-symbol semantics, XML/reference ownership, source/default/nullability compatibility review, independently pinned adoption and task-scoped real AOT/consumer evidence. Templates do not authorize product implementation or silently inherit across repositories.

limits: This note is not GitHub approval or formal contract acceptance.
The package generator emits limited static shape metadata, not production ORM mapping or Server dispatch.
Actual AOT execution covers the retained Linux research codec/package-flow slice only; Windows/product execution is not inferred.
No pristine host-image claim is made; the effective consumer PATH and no-Rust invocation are the demonstrated boundary.
Production package closure enforcement, output-location loader, signing, all IDE hosts and complete product behavior remain assigned Delivery obligations.
The review did not rerun upstream Rust/.NET suites or replace preserved source research.
